chunks: From him, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from Rifāʿah, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about wudu (ablution) in the mosque, and he disliked it when it was due to urination or defecation.

key_terms.الْمَسْجِدِ: the mosque, the sacred place of worship
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual washing for taharah
key_terms.فَكَرِهَهُ: he disliked it; indicating reprehensibility or disapproval

ai.seo_question: Is it disliked to perform wudu in the mosque after urination or defecation?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling on performing wudu (ablution) in the mosque when it is occasioned by relieving oneself. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام expresses dislike for this, indicating an etiquette and legal discouragement connected to preserving the sanctity and cleanliness of the mosque.
